group.passage: Xiaoliuqiu is a small coral island off the southwest coast of Taiwan, about 30 minutes by boat from Donggang. Many visitors come here with one special hope: to see a green sea turtle, or even to swim next to one. Green sea turtles get their name from the color of their fat, not their shells. Adult turtles eat mostly seaweed and sea grass, and many of them feed in the shallow water around the island. Because fishing nets have been banned near the island, the number of turtles living there has grown in recent years. In 2023, the Ocean Conservation Administration counted an average of 637 turtles a month in the waters around Xiaoliuqiu. Between May and October, female turtles also come ashore, crawling up onto the island's beaches to lay their eggs in the sand. Divers and snorkelers now play an important part in protecting the turtles. Since 2017, a group called TurtleSpot Taiwan has asked people to send in photos of the turtles they meet. The key is the turtle's face. The size, shape, and arrangement of the scales around each turtle's eyes are different, much like human fingerprints. By comparing photos, researchers can tell one turtle from another and learn where each one lives. The photos also help them check whether a hurt turtle has become healthy again after being released, and how many turtles have been injured by fishing lines. Visitors, however, must follow some rules. Sea turtles are protected by law in Taiwan, so people must not touch, chase, or feed them. Anyone who disturbs a turtle can be sent to prison for up to one year or fined up to NT$300,000. Local groups also clean up trash on the beaches so that mother turtles have a safe place to lay their eggs. With this help from many people, Xiaoliuqiu has become one of the best places in Taiwan to see these gentle animals.

translation_zh.text:
小琉球是台灣西南海岸外的一座小珊瑚島，從東港搭船大約 30 分鐘。許多遊客帶著一個特別的希望來到這裡：看到綠蠵龜，甚至在牠旁邊游泳。
綠蠵龜的名字來自牠們脂肪的顏色，而不是牠們的殼。成年海龜主要吃海藻和海草，其中許多會在島嶼周圍的淺水區覓食。由於島嶼附近已經禁止使用漁網，近年來住在那裡的海龜數量增加了。2023 年，海洋保育署在小琉球周圍海域平均每月記錄到 637 隻海龜。每年 5 月到 10 月之間，母海龜也會上岸，爬上島上的海灘，在沙裡產卵。
潛水員和浮潛的人現在在保護海龜這件事上扮演重要的角色。從 2017 年起，一個名叫 TurtleSpot Taiwan 的團體請大家把遇到的海龜照片寄給他們。關鍵在於海龜的臉。每隻海龜眼睛周圍鱗片的大小、形狀和排列都不一樣，就像人類的指紋一樣。研究人員比對照片，就能分辨不同的海龜，並知道每一隻住在哪裡。這些照片也幫助他們確認受傷的海龜在野放後是否恢復健康，以及有多少海龜被釣魚線弄傷。
不過，遊客必須遵守一些規定。海龜在台灣受到法律保護，所以人們不可以觸摸、追逐或餵食牠們。任何干擾海龜的人，最高可處一年徒刑或新台幣 30 萬元罰款。當地團體也會清理海灘上的垃圾，讓母海龜有安全的地方產卵。在許多人的幫助下，小琉球已經成為台灣觀賞這些溫和動物最好的地方之一。

Visitors may see or swim with green sea turtles（核對：f2；同上）
Green turtles are named for the color of their fat; adults eat mostly seaweed and sea grass（核對：f5；NOAA Fisheries 核對）
Many turtles feed in the shallow water around the island（核對：事實單沒有這一條；外部資料（Ng & Balazs 2012 小琉球實地報告：綠蠵龜在近岸淺水礁岩藻床覓食）支持，與事實不矛盾；不涉及任何題目答案）
Fishing nets banned near the island, so turtle numbers grew（核對：f3；大鵬灣頁：Due to the ban on fishing net, the green sea turtle population at the island has increased）
In 2023 the Ocean Conservation Administration counted an average of 637 turtles a month（核對：f4；Taipei Times 2024-07-17：an average of 637 sea turtles were recorded per month last year）
Females come ashore to nest from May to October（核對：f6；Taipei Times 2024-07-17：from May to October）
TurtleSpot Taiwan has asked people to send turtle photos since 2017（核對：f7；Taipei Times 2026-09-17：established in 2017）
Scales around each turtle's eyes differ like fingerprints（核對：f8；同上）
Photos help check recovery of released injured turtles and how many were injured by fishing lines（核對：f9；來源寫 entanglement in fishing gear（漁具纏繞），文中寫 fishing lines（釣線，屬漁具的一種），範圍略窄但不矛盾）
Protected by law; do not touch, chase, or feed（核對：f10；Taipei Times 2026-09-17（touch, chase）、Focus Taiwan 2026-04-27（do not feed））
Disturbing a turtle: up to one year in prison or a fine up to NT$300,000（核對：f11；Taipei Times：up to one year in prison, detention or a fine of up to NT$300,000）
Local groups clean beach trash so mother turtles can nest（核對：f12；Taipei Times 2024-07-17）
Xiaoliuqiu is one of the best places in Taiwan to see sea turtles（核對：f13；Focus Taiwan：one of Taiwan's best-known habitats）
